finding.claim: dropTable ignores the error returned by Authorize, so any authenticated user (any role) can execute DROP TABLE.
finding.source: Any authenticated request to /admin/drop (user from request context, roles unchecked)

trace.note: Authorize(u, "dba") called but its error return is discarded
runSQL executes DROP TABLE regardless of the authorization result

finding.guards_checked: Authorize (api.go:13-20) returns 'forbidden' for non-dba users, but the result is never checked at line 26. No other guard in this handler. vacuum (api.go:33-36) shows the intended check, which is absent here.
finding.repro: Authenticate as a user with roles ["user"] and send GET or POST /admin/drop?t=<existing_table>. The handler drops the table and returns 204.

verdict.guard_found: Authorize (api.go:13-20) returns "forbidden" for users without the "dba" role, but its result is discarded at api.go:26 as a bare statement, so it blocks nothing. No other guard exists in dropTable (api.go:24-29) or on the route registration (api.go:44). Authentication that populates the "user" context value is not in this file and could not be checked.
verdict.reason: Authorize's error is discarded at api.go:26 and runSQL("DROP TABLE " + r.FormValue("t")) runs unconditionally at api.go:27, so any caller whose context carries a user (any role) reaches the drop, while vacuum (api.go:33-36) shows the check that was intended. The trace matches the code at every cited line; the only unverified piece is the authentication middleware, which is outside this file.

finding.claim: Table name from the request is concatenated into a SQL statement without validation or quoting, enabling SQL injection.
finding.source: r.FormValue("t") at api.go:27 (URL query or form body, attacker-controlled)

trace.note: attacker-controlled t is concatenated into the SQL string passed to runSQL
runSQL is a stub here; real implementation not in repo, so stacked-statement execution is unverified

finding.guards_checked: No validation, allowlist, identifier quoting, or parameterization on t. The authorization bypass in F1 makes this reachable by any authenticated user. Even with F1 fixed, a dba user could inject additional statements.
finding.repro: As any authenticated user: GET /admin/drop?t=x;DROP+TABLE+y (or other crafted identifier). Impact depends on whether runSQL permits multiple statements.

verdict.guard_found: Authorize at api.go:13-20 is the only role control, but its error return is discarded as a bare statement at api.go:26, so it does not block the request. No validation, allowlist, identifier quoting, or parameterization exists on r.FormValue("t") at api.go:27. runSQL at api.go:41 is an empty stub, so the sink's real behavior (including whether stacked statements run) is unverified.
verdict.reason: The request reaches dropTable via /admin/drop (api.go:44) with any user already in context, the role check at api.go:26 is a discarded return value so it never aborts, and the attacker-controlled t is concatenated unescaped into the SQL at api.go:27 with no effective control; the injection pattern is real, though its full impact depends on the unseen runSQL implementation.

finding.claim: Destructive DDL is triggerable through GET or cross-site requests because the handler accepts query parameters and has no method restriction or CSRF token. Plausible; depends on unseen auth middleware.
finding.source: t parameter via r.FormValue (accepts URL query and POST body) at api.go:27; route registered without method check at api.go:44

trace.note: /admin/drop registered with no method or CSRF enforcement
FormValue reads t from the URL query, so a GET from a cross-site link, image, or form can carry the request
Authorization is not enforced (see F1), so any session-authenticated browser triggers the drop

finding.guards_checked: No CSRF token, Origin/Referer check, or method restriction in this file. Whether the auth middleware uses cookies (and therefore is exposed to CSRF) is not verifiable from this repo.
finding.repro: Host an HTML page containing and get a logged-in browser session to load it. Unverified: depends on cookie-based auth in middleware not present here.

verdict.guard_found: Authorize(u, "dba") at api.go:26 is the only authorization control. It returns an error, but the call is a bare statement and the result is discarded, so it blocks nothing. The vacuum handler at api.go:33-36 checks the result correctly, which shows the intended pattern. No method check or CSRF token exists in api.go:24-29 or the route at api.go:44. The auth middleware that sets the "user" context value is not in this repo.
verdict.reason: Authorize's error is discarded at api.go:26, so any authenticated user with no "dba" role reaches runSQL("DROP TABLE " + r.FormValue("t")) at api.go:27 via a direct request to /admin/drop (route at api.go:44, which accepts any method and reads query params). The CSRF/GET-from-a-third-party-page path depends on cookie-based auth in unseen middleware and remains unverifiable, but the authorization bypass alone is confirmed.
